subject: financial-literacy
instructions: Use only the fictional or supplied figures. Do not disclose household income, accounts, balances, or spending.
Show computations for fixed items and explain the tradeoff or decision for open items.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain ways people earn income in your own words and give or identify a valid example.
Use a diagram, model, quotation, data display, map, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of skills and education.
Apply gross and take-home concepts in a new realistic situation. Show the process or cite evidence.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, unsafe choice, or design flaw involving entrepreneurship; correct it and explain why.
Connect ways people earn income with workplace responsibility. Explain how the ideas support, constrain, contrast with, or build on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit project: Design a fictional age-appropriate service or micro-enterprise plan using safe, legal, guardian-approved assumptions.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy or quality, and one next question.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated accuracy or fidelity criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated evidence and reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated application or performance criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated checking and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Earning and Work?
